speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; please describe the skin condition you are experiencing on the back of your left hand, including when it started and any symptoms you have noticed. To help narrow this down, have you had any recent insect bites, exposure to new plants, or contact with chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your age and outdoor activities, do the lesions on the back of your left hand appear as rough, scaly patches or as distinct, open sores? Additionally, have you noticed any recent changes in your blood sugar control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of an elderly patient with sun exposure history is classic for Actinic Keratosis, a precursor to squamous cell carcinoma. While your diabetes and hypertension are noted, they are not the primary cause of this specific skin finding. I have determined the diagnosis based on your description and clinical presentation; no further tests are required at this time.
